title: Relaxed Load for Loop Condition (Stale Cache Stall)
pattern: Spinning on an atomic variable load with `Ordering::Relaxed` in a tight loop without intermediate synchronization barriers.
why_bad: While correct under a sequentially consistent cache coherency model, some hardware architectures (and optimization-aggressive compilers) can delay flushing store buffers or invalidating cache lines, stalling the spinning thread for an unpredictable duration.
detection: A `while` loop condition consisting entirely of an atomic load with `Relaxed` ordering and an empty or near-empty loop body.
counterexample: The loop contains an explicit hardware instruction yield (like `spin_loop::hint`) or uses `Acquire` ordering combined with a memory fence.
source: Paul McKenney Appendix C, Jon Gjengset Ch 9
